requirements.summary: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with `daily` directive, validated syntax with `logrotate -d` (no errors), and confirmed logrotate.timer is active/enabled with a scheduled next run both before and after a node restart, providing the system-level daily cadence enforcement.

Config specifies `rotate 7` and `compress` (with `delaycompress`). Two forced rotations were performed and directly observed: first rotation produced an uncompressed app.log.1, second rotation compressed that prior file to app.log.2.gz, confirming the compress/delaycompress chain works as configured and is consistent with the 7-rotation retention count.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing to the log after rotation
requirements.summary: copytruncate was used specifically to avoid breaking an open file handle. Directly verified: inode number (290759) was captured before rotation and confirmed unchanged after rotation via `stat -c '%i'`, and new content was successfully appended and captured in a subsequent rotation, proving the writer could continue writing to the same file post-rotation.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of public task contract)
requirements.summary: Healthy pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id 636556ce..., uptime-since 08:24:55, config/log/timer state), reboot acknowledged before disconnection, outage observed via connection timeouts/resets, then reconnection with a different boot_id (3e7264d8...) and reset uptime, followed by post-restart verification that config, log content, and timer state were all recovered intact. Cross-checked against the fixed after_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots, which independently confirm the same boot_id transition.

overall_summary: The executor configured /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily/rotate 7/compress/delaycompress/copytruncate and directly demonstrated, via two forced rotations, that the file's inode is preserved (continuous writability) and that compression/retention chaining works as intended. All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence rather than config-only claims. The separately mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently executed: healthy pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, observed outage, changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of config/log/timer state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Test artifacts from validation rotations were cleaned up and the log restored to baseline content, leaving no residue.
limitations: No evidence of a real 7-day rotation cycle or of the timer actually firing autonomously (only two manually forced rotations were observed); reliance is on config text plus timer-active/enabled status for the ongoing daily cadence.
Restart evidence protocol was performed once for the single managed node (node1), consistent with the single-node topology; no additional nodes existed to cross-check.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace clearly to task outcomes or bounded, restored validation: creating the logrotate config (kept, required), two forced rotations used to prove copytruncate inode preservation and compress/delaycompress chaining (test artifacts app.log.1 and app.log.2.gz, plus logrotate.status, were fully removed and app.log content restored to its original baseline in cmd-7aa8f32960ae487f), and the mandated single reboot for the restart-evidence protocol. No unnecessary or unrestored residue was found; after_executor listening-sockets/temp-file diffs are explained entirely by the reboot (new PIDs, new systemd-private dirs, /tmp/reboot.log from the backgrounded reboot wrapper) rather than any leftover application state.
